bc_hang_dog_hill.blurb: Hang Dog Hill is a small crag in the Southern Crags section of Skaha Bluffs, in the Okanagan. It holds eight short climbs, almost all of them bolted sport lines with a single trad route mixed in. Difficulty stays gentle, from 5.7 up to 5.10, with 5.9 being the most common grade, so it suits newer leaders and anyone setting up top-ropes. The routes are brief and easy-going rather than sustained. The crag sits just above the trail on the left, a short walk past the trailhead gate toward the Daycare area.

bc_the_change_room.blurb: The Change Room is a set of single-pitch crags perched above the Stained Walls at Harrison Bluffs in the Fraser Valley. All eight routes here are trad climbs, and they cover a wide spread: a couple at 5.8, one 5.9, three at 5.10, and two hard 5.12 lines. The walls face south, so they pick up plenty of sun. Reaching them takes a committed walk on ledges, fixed ropes and a flagged scrambling trail, so expect more effort than at the lower walls.

bc_low_tide.blurb: Low Tide is a lakeside bouldering zone within the Beachside group near Arrow Lake in the West Kootenay. It has eight problems, ranging from V0 to a standout V9, with the middle of the range around V3. The lines are described as attractive and not too tall. Because Arrow Lake is a reservoir, the blocks go underwater at high water, around June and July, so the season is shorter than at nearby zones. The boulders are scattered, and you can reach them by working west along the beach from the main Beachside boulder.

bc_ponderosa_2.blurb: Ponderosa is a bouldering zone high above the shore of Arrow Lake in the West Kootenay, set among ponderosa pines. The original boulder found here offers face climbing and works well as a warm-up before heading uphill to the much bigger Fukushima Boulder. It has eight problems, mostly easy to moderate, with several at V2 and a handful at V1 or below, plus one around V4. The walk in is the longest of any zone at Arrow Lake, climbing a steep trail.
